locator: I q.4 a.2 co.: in Deo sunt perfectiones omnium rerum. Unde et dicitur universaliter perfectus
interpretation: God is called universally perfect because no nobility found in any genus is absent from him. The first proof distinguishes possession in the same account from preexistence in a cause in a more eminent way; it concludes that all perfections preexist in God eminently. The existing IsPerfect reading quantifies over perfection-respects of InAct, whose formal-or-virtual interpretation is required; it does not attribute mutually opposed creaturely forms to God in their creaturely manner.
